scope_description: Current-state audit of Bee harness parity between Pi and Claude Code at 50c90045. Includes the completed Pi support, belt parity, result mailbox, worktree relocation, harness workflow parity, and workflow-tail parity features. Reviews the shipped Pi extension, shared CLI, onboarding, dispatch transport, context and skill loading, lifecycle tests, and named host-capability exclusions. Excludes OMP and unrelated feature changes.

reviewer_manifest.reason: The required reviewer dispatch resolved to an Agent-tool payload, but the active Pi harness exposes no Agent tool. The lead completed a disclosed local audit instead; this record is not an independent multi-agent wave.

verification_preflight.result: passed; 3,551 core tests and 61 Pi contract tests passed
verification_preflight.scope_note: Fresh full-suite proof plus direct source and locked-decision audit across the six frozen Pi features. Independent lenses remain uncovered because dispatch could not execute.

findings.title: Pi receives a Claude dispatch command in its injected session preamble
findings.detail: build_session_preamble always renders dispatch_door_lines for runtime claude. The Pi belt injects that same preamble through session-init. A Pi agent therefore bypasses team.pi and receives a native Agent payload that Pi cannot execute; this review reproduced that exact failure when reviewer dispatch returned Agent but no Agent tool existed. The Pi end-to-end test hides the defect by hand-writing --runtime pi and never asserting the injected preamble. This violates pi-support D5/D8 and blocks the required worker path for every non-tiny workflow.

findings.title: Pi activity exclusions claim that documented lifecycle carriers do not exist
findings.detail: The belt names PreToolUse, PermissionRequest, and Notification activity as exclusions because Pi allegedly has no advisory pre-tool or prompt event. Pi 0.84.4 documents tool_execution_start before tool_call and ui_prompt_start/ui_prompt_end around blocking UI prompts. The belt registers neither event, so a Pi session can remain working while it waits for user input. docs/config-reference.md:272-274 repeats the false capability claim, and the parity test validates only that an exclusion comment exists, not that its reason is true.

findings.title: Workflow close can race a planned-next handoff and hide live claim authority
findings.detail: close_workflow_records preflights mailbox records without a handoff lock, releases no transaction boundary across pause clearing and workflow closure, and closes later through separate workflow locks. write_mailbox_handoff checks its prerequisites before taking only handoff:<workflow-id> and does not re-check workflow status. A writer can therefore add planned-next after close preflight, or after close while it holds a previously resolved workflow id. Close succeeds, projection rebuild omits the closed workflow, and live planned-next authority becomes inaccessible. This violates D4/D6 and plan.md:194, which requires workflow and handoff locks in documented order.

findings.title: The runtime health command does not support Pi
findings.detail: Runtime contains only Claude and Codex. Fresh execution of bee doctor --runtime pi --json returns unsupported_argument_shape. Pi onboarding, extension presence, skill discovery, and runtime readiness therefore have no equivalent fail-closed health report, although Claude has one. This is an operational parity gap, not a named host-capability exclusion.

decision.summary: Current Pi support is not feature-equivalent to Claude Code: P1 2, P2 2, P3 0. Core tests pass, but the injected dispatch route is unusable on Pi and workflow-close claim safety is not transactional.
decision.next_action: Fix F1 and F3, re-run the Pi end-to-end path from the injected preamble, then run an independent delta review.
